theme: Restaurant and leisure proxies: OpenTable state of the industry CSV, Yelp dataset, Google Maps reviews scrapers, event ticket data
queries_run: gh search repos "opentable state of industry"
gh search repos "google maps reviews scraper"

candidates.name: OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs (data/ folder): 'Womply - {City,County,State,National} - Weekly.csv' (small-business revenue/merchants-open index by industry incl. restaurants/food service, from Womply, 2020-2023), 'Affinity - {City,County,State,National} - {Daily,Monthly}.csv' (credit/debit card spend by category incl. Arts & Entertainment, Restaurants & Hotels, Grocery), 'Google Mobility - ... .csv' (retail/recreation mobility by county/state/city), 'Employment - ...Weekly.csv', 'Job Postings - ...Weekly.csv', 'UI Claims', 'COVID - ... Daily.csv', GeoIDs crosswalks. US geography, county/city/state/national grain, primarily 2020-01 through ~2023 (some series stop mid-2023); actively maintained repo (pushed 2026-09-12), 341 stars, no explicit license file (attribution-required per README, check terms before quoting). This is the repo behind tracktherecovery.org. Verified via `gh api repos/.../contents/data` listing (48 files) and a code search inside the repo: current file set does NOT contain a standalone 'OpenTable' file (OpenTable stopped supplying data to this tracker; Womply is the closest surviving restaurant/small-business proxy).
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #6 (public consumer-spend panels; the gap list explicitly names 'OpenTable seated diners' alongside this exact project) and doubles as a leisure/restaurant/entertainment demand proxy (Affinity card-spend 'Arts & Entertainment' and 'Restaurants & Hotels' categories, Womply restaurant revenue, Google Mobility 'retail & recreation') that could nowcast US regional consumer leisure strength feeding into ABNB nights/ADR by region. Caveat: series thin out after 2023, so utility is mostly historical/backtest, not current nowcasting — flag for the team to check the live tracktherecovery.org site vs. this repo's freshness before relying on it for 2026 quarters.
candidates.time_coverage: 2020-01 to ~2023-06 for most series (repo itself last pushed 2026-09-12; unclear if data files still update)
candidates.size_hint: 48 CSV/CSV.GZ files in data/, multi-MB each
candidates.license: none declared (custom attribution terms in README)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps loosely with held BEA PCE travel panel and OECD consumer confidence, but this is higher-frequency (weekly/daily) and county-level, and is the specific project the gap list names — worth a closer look even though OpenTable itself is gone from it.

candidates.name: sosedoff/opentable
candidates.what_it_holds: Ruby client wrapping OpenTable's (unofficial) restaurant-search and reservation-availability endpoints; 142 stars, updated 2026-08-15, no data committed, license 'other' (check terms before use).
candidates.why_useful: A live client for pulling current OpenTable restaurant availability/booking data (a real-time seated-diners/leisure-demand proxy, gap #6) rather than a historical panel; would need to be run going forward to build a time series, and ToS for automated pulls from OpenTable is a human call per repo rules.

candidates.name: georgekhananaev/google-reviews-scraper-pro
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/MongoDB Google Maps review scraper: multi-language review extraction, incremental scraping, image downloads, anti-detection handling; 329 stars, MIT license, updated 2026-09-10 (actively maintained).
candidates.why_useful: A working, actively-maintained method to build a time series of review volume/ratings for restaurants, attractions, and short-term-rental-adjacent leisure businesses in specific markets (proxy for local leisure/tourism activity levels feeding nights/ADR by region); scrapes Google, not Airbnb, so it is a methods-only flag per the run rules, not to be executed here.

candidates.name: omkarcloud/google-maps-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python Google Maps reviews scraper for sentiment/trend extraction from business reviews; 182 stars, MIT license, updated 2026-09-09.
candidates.why_useful: Same class of tool as above — could be pointed at restaurants/attractions/hotels in ABNB-relevant markets to build a leisure-activity/engagement proxy series; no data committed, method only.

candidates.name: omarshahine/restaurant-cli
candidates.what_it_holds: Pluggable CLI/agent-skill for booking restaurant reservations across Resy, OpenTable, Tock, SevenRooms from one codebase; 8 stars, MIT, updated 2026-09-02.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: built for booking, not data collection, but the same API-plugin layer could in principle be adapted to poll availability across multiple reservation platforms as a leisure-demand proxy; flagged as a low-confidence lead only.

notes: Hard search-call budget (6 gh search repos calls) burned mostly on the literal keyword hints (opentable, yelp dataset, google maps reviews scraper) which are dominated by generic Kaggle/academic-Yelp-dataset ML tutorial notebooks (excluded per instructions — none commit the Yelp dataset itself, all require the user's own download from yelp.com/dataset under Yelp's own licence) and by hundreds of near-identical Apify-actor-wrapper 'google-maps-reviews-scraper' repos (kept only the two most-starred, actively maintained ones). 'foursquare checkin dataset' and 'ticketmaster events dataset' both returned zero hits via gh search repos; a check of the foursquare GitHub org found no open-places dataset repo there (Foursquare's 2024 Open Source Places release, if on GitHub, is not under that org name — worth a follow-up scout with a fresh search budget). WebSearch was already exhausted (200/200) for this session before I could run any site:github.com queries, so this scout leaned on WebFetch (no API cost) plus gh api contents/metadata calls on repos I already suspected existed. The one real find, OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker, is the specific project CONTEXT.md gap #6 calls out by name — it is live and well-maintained but no longer carries OpenTable data specifically (confirmed via a code search inside the repo); its Womply/Affinity/Google-Mobility files are the closest surviving restaurant/leisure proxy and are worth a teammate's closer look with the full data dictionary. Event-ticket data (Ticketmaster/StubHub/Songkick/Eventbrite) and a genuine OpenTable 'state of the industry' CSV mirror were not found in this pass — recommend a re-run with a fresh WebSearch budget targeting site:github.com queries for 'eventbrite api dataset', 'songkick concerts scraper', 'stubhub api python', and 'opentable state of industry github' once the shared search quota resets.
